sources.title: Parliament of Ghana: History of Parliament
sources.note: Official timeline: independence in 1957, republic and ten women MPs in 1960, coups and constitutional return in 1993.

sources.title: Judicial Service of Ghana: Constitution of 1992, Article 1
sources.note: Original English constitutional text. Short quotation reproduced exactly; explanation is a plain-English gloss, not a different-language translation.

sources.title: UNESCO: Craftsmanship of traditional woven textile Kente
sources.note: 2024 inscription: strip weaving, named patterns, apprenticeship and chief weavers. Do not assign one modern production pattern to all historical communities.

sources.title: Smithsonian National Museum of African Art: Red Pepper Coffin
sources.note: Paa Joe, circa 1992; Teshi-Nungua context, materials and restricted rather than universal use. Direct si.edu endpoint failed; museum subdomain full indexed entry checked.

sources.title: Smithsonian: Samuel Narh Nartey, Nokia cellphone coffin
sources.note: 2007 museum exhibition commission, not an excavated burial. Artist trained 11 years with Paa Joe.

sources.title: UNICEF Ghana: Girls changing rooms and modern urinals
sources.note: 2021 report on named pupils and school facilities;101 urinals/changing rooms in four districts, over 10,000 schoolgirls.

sources.title: WHO: Malaria vaccine pilot launched in Ghana
sources.note: 2 May 2019 report on 30 April launch; Susana and Abigail first Ghana pilot recipients, alongside Ghana/Kenya/Malawi programme. Dated historical event, not current medical advice.

sources.title: Volta River Authority: Akosombo Hydro Plant
sources.note: Plant facts: construction 1961 to 1965; hydroelectric power and dam/lake system.

sources.title: Stephan F. Miescher: Ghana’s Akosombo Dam, Volta Lake Fisheries and Climate Change
sources.note: Daedalus historical research: Worobong to Amate resettlement inOctober 1964; technical achievement and displacement both examined.

sources.title: United Nations Digital Library: Congo country-name history
sources.note: Authority-record history: independence on 30 June 1960, DRC in 1964, Zaire in 1971, DRC restored in 1997.

sources.title: UN Peacekeeping: Why have UN peacekeepers been in DR Congo for 65 years?
sources.note: 2025 institutional historical account: independence crisis, Mobutu dictatorship, wars of 1996 to 1997 and 1998 to 2003, continuing armed violence. Indexed account checked; direct access returned 403.

sources.title: Presidency of DRC: Constitution, revised edition of 2011
sources.note: Journal Officiel page 8, Article 1: motto and language provisions. Historical dated constitutional text; no claim about present compliance.

sources.title: UNESCO: Congolese rumba
sources.note: 2021 multinational inscription for both Congo states; transmission and social uses. Indexed full entry checked when direct route served an empty application shell.

sources.title: Museum of Modern Art: Bodys Isek Kingelez, City Dreams
sources.note: 2018 exhibition: found materials, Kimbembele Ihunga 1994 and Ville Fantome 1996. Models represent proposals and imagination, not constructed cities.

sources.title: UNICEF: Safe water for students and families in Walungu
sources.note: 5 December 2022 report: Chirhavanyi Primary School water in 2021, Asifiwe, and Izenge Health Centre family experience. Local improvements, not a national coverage estimate.

sources.title: IITA: New project to strengthen and modernize DRC’s cassava sector
sources.note: 2023 project launch. Breadmaking and substitution are project objectives, not achieved universal adoption.

sources.title: Norwegian Nobel Committee: 2018 Peace Prize announcement
sources.note: Official announcement supports award, hospital work and 1999 foundation. Indexed text checked; direct fetch 403. Separate Nobel Facts page incorrectly gives 2008 and is not used.

sources.title: Cameroon Ministry of Tourism: Independence and reunification
sources.note: Official historical account, independence on 1 January 1960 and political consolidation; read alongside UN documentation rather than treating official interpretation as neutral.

sources.title: United Nations Yearbook 1961: Cameroons under British administration
sources.note: Contemporary institutional account of separate northern and southern plebiscites and the June and October 1961 outcomes.

sources.title: Presidency of Cameroon: Organisation de l’Etat
sources.note: Official French description of the 1996 constitutional provisions, equal official languages and motto. Translation of the three-word motto supplied in English.

sources.title: UNESCO: Nguon, rituals of governance in the Bamoun community
sources.note: 2023 inscription describes consultation, public trial, celebrations and transmission. This is a particular community practice, not the national electoral system.

sources.title: Library of Congress: Competing Cartographies in Cameroon
sources.note: Amelia Raines, 1 February 2023, on Njoya’s Bamum maps and the map acquired in 2021. Earlier objects discussed as heritage preserved in modern times.

sources.title: UNICEF Cameroon: Digital innovation in Melong through the e-container
sources.note: 25 June 2025 report; named pupil Eyong Blessing, recycled solar-powered hub, teacher training and demand for places.

sources.title: UNICEF Cameroon: Alahlie’s safe-water story
sources.note: 16 September 2025 account of solar borehole, named pupil and displaced mother, community maintenance and regional conflict.

sources.title: Smithsonian National Postal Museum: Cameroon
sources.note: Institutional chronology and postal evidence for changing political designations, including the 1972 United Republic.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: Senegal
sources.note: Diplomatic chronology distinguishes independence from France and Senegal’s withdrawal from the Mali Federation on 20 August 1960.

sources.title: US Department of State: Senegal background note, February 1998
sources.note: Archived historical account used only for the 1960 federation and 1981 succession, not as a current assessment.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General: West Africa and the Sahel report S/2024/521
sources.note: 2024 report describes pre-election tensions and democratic transfer of power in Senegal.

sources.title: Presidency of Senegal: Flag and motto
sources.note: French national motto reproduced with spaced hyphens replacing typographic dashes. Translation supplied; a national ideal, not a statement that citizens have identical beliefs.

sources.title: UNESCO: Ceebu Jën, a culinary art of Senegal
sources.note: 2021 inscription describes ingredients, family transmission and meal etiquette, with regional variation.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Iba Ndiaye, Between Latitude and Longitude
sources.note: Exhibition research, artist biography and Tabaski III (1970), oil on plywood, 150 by 250 cm.

sources.title: UNICEF Senegal: Menstruation should not interrupt a girl’s education
sources.note: 27 May 2022 reporting from Kaffrine; Nogaye and Ndela among 47 trainees sewing reusable pads, ten-day training and 20,900 produced.

sources.title: Institut Pasteur de Dakar: Programmes and laboratory services
sources.note: Institution’s own description of yellow-fever vaccine manufacture, surveillance network and food/water laboratory work. Avoid undelivered expansion targets and inconsistent changing statistics.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: Mali
sources.note: Independence and dissolution of the Mali Federation in 1960; distinct from medieval Mali.

sources.title: United Nations: Mali’s transitional government crisis, May 2021
sources.note: Contemporary account links the August 2020 overthrow and May 2021 detention of transitional leaders.

sources.title: US Department of State: Relations with Mali, archived 2022 account
sources.note: Used for 2012 rebellion and coup only. Archived membership and diplomatic statements are not treated as current.

sources.title: Jalada Africa: Bamanankan translation by Ismaila Samba Traoré
sources.note: 2016 primary publication of a Bamanankan translation of Ngũgĩ wa Thiong’o’s story. Exact published title, English counterpart and translator’s biography checked. This is modern translated literature, not an ancient inscription.

sources.title: UNESCO: Djenné communities conserving their heritage
sources.note: 30 June 2025 eyewitness institutional account of replastering on 25 May and 12 June, materials, masons and public participation.

sources.title: UNESCO: Bamako conference on safeguarding Mali’s manuscripts
sources.note: 2015 conference account: manuscripts rescued from Timbuktu in 2012, family libraries, boxes and digitization. Avoid treating temporary Bamako location as still universal.

sources.title: UNESCO: Masks and puppets in Markala
sources.note: 2014 inscription: named communities, initiation, post-harvest celebration, fishing and reconciliation. Full indexed description checked.

sources.title: UNESCO decision 6.COM 13.29: Senufo balafon practices
sources.note: 2011 decision describes keys, gourd resonators, membranes and children’s instruments. Cultural practice crosses state borders.

sources.title: UNICEF Mali: Every piece matters
sources.note: 30 April 2019, Anne Kennedy; named teacher Fatoumata Barry and pupil Ada Diagayété, Sévaré stadium shelter and sanitation. Ada’s age differs between text and captions, so omit it.

sources.title: US diplomatic documents: Recognition of Guinea, 1958
sources.note: Editorial note records National Assembly proclamation on 2 October 1958 and establishment of relations.

sources.title: Human Rights Watch: Guinea, We Have Lived in Darkness
sources.note: 2011 research report with historical background on Touré’s 1958 to 1984 dictatorship and subsequent governments. Use restrained, non-graphic account.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General: Guinea presidential election process, 3 December 2010
sources.note: Certification of 2010 runoff; dated event rather than a permanent characterization of the political system.

sources.title: African Union Peace and Security Council: Guinea, 22 January 2026
sources.note: AU primary decision lifting suspension after the December 2025 presidential election. Do not repeat its evaluative praise as independent proof of political freedoms.

sources.title: United Nations: Accountability and Guinea’s political transition
sources.note: 2021 statement dates the military coup to 5 September; graphic descriptions not reproduced.

sources.title: Richard Ishida: N’Ko orthography notes
sources.note: Technical orthography reference by a writing-systems specialist: exact name ߒߞߏ, meaning I say, script direction and Manding usage.

sources.title: Unicode Standard, chapter 19: N’Ko
sources.note: Section 19.4: Solomana Kanté’s 1949 script, vowel and tone notation, right-to-left direction. Original sample separately checked in Ishida.

sources.title: UNESCO: Cultural space of Sosso-Bala
sources.note: Modern safeguarding account of the instrument, Dökala family and children’s learning. Medieval origin is a community historical tradition, not a modern laboratory dating result.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: D’mba headdress, 1979.206.17
sources.note: Historical wooden object, late nineteenth to first half twentieth century; Baga ideals of motherhood, costume and performance. Explicitly contextualized as inherited heritage.

sources.title: WHO: Final results of Guinea’s Ebola vaccine trial
sources.note: 23 December 2016 report on 2015 ring trial; historical research findings, not personal medical guidance or blanket efficacy guarantee.

sources.title: UNICEF Guinea: Restoring water and latrines at Danéné school
sources.note: 15 June 2021 report, N’zérékoré; borehole and four-cubicle block, parents’ association president Gabriel Sagno.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: Niger
sources.note: Recognition and independence on 3 August 1960; distinguish Niger from neighboring Nigeria.

sources.title: US Department of State: Niger background note, September 2008
sources.note: Archived chronology used for Hamani Diori, 1974 coup and the 1991 national conference, not current politics. Full indexed history checked.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General: Unconstitutional change of government in Niger
sources.note: 26 July 2023 statement; dated military takeover and condemnation.

sources.title: United Nations Niger: Country Team report 2023
sources.note: Institutional report summary says the July crisis and sanctions affected development prospects and programme planning.

sources.title: World Resources Institute: Radio helps Niger farmers restore their land
sources.note: Lucas Toh, Salima Mahamoudou and John-Rob Pool, 7 August 2018; primary project reporting on Ali Malam, Sakina Mati and Radio Zumunci.

sources.title: UNESCO: Practices and expressions of joking relationships in Niger
sources.note: 2014 inscription describes recognized relationships, mutual duties and peaceful dispute settlement; not permission to mock strangers.

sources.title: UNESCO: Imzad practices in Algeria, Mali and Niger
sources.note: 2013 inscription; women makers and players, gourd body, bow, poetry and oral learning. Full indexed description checked after direct page returned interface only.

sources.title: Niger Ministry of Hydraulics: J’apprends l’hygiène avec Amina et Amadou
sources.note: March 2009 Tahoua village-water project booklet for CE 2/CM 1 pupils; primary educational artifact. Characters are fictional, prescriptions are educational aims rather than a survey of actual school conditions. PDF contains imposed booklet pages; use printed page numbers.

sources.title: African Union UN Mission: Federal Republic of Somalia
sources.note: Official state profile, updated February 2026; formation of the republic on 1 July 1960 and 1961 constitution.

sources.title: Somali Upper House: Historical Background
sources.note: Institutional history: 1969 coup, 1991 collapse, transitional institutions, 2012 constitution and first functioning Senate in 2016. English has grammatical mistakes; do not copy its erroneous use of since for until.

sources.title: UN DPPA: Khaled Khiari’s Security Council briefing, 29 December 2025
sources.note: Full indexed official briefing checked; direct fetch failed. Records Israeli recognition on 26 December, Somali objection, AU position and Security Council affirmation of Somalia’s sovereignty. Do not treat a country representative’s statement as the UN’s own position.

sources.title: World Bank: Appraisal of a Third Education Project in the Somali Democratic Republic, 1977
sources.note: Report 1334-SO, 26 July 1977, Appendix II pages 1 to 2. Contemporary education appraisal; government literacy percentages are not independently established and are omitted.

sources.title: Jalada Africa: Kacaanka Jira, Somali translation, 2016
sources.note: Primary publication, 22 March 2016; exact title, Somali label, two translators and linked English counterpart. Modern translation of Ngũgĩ’s story, not an ancient Somali text.

sources.title: Michele Nori: The golden Udder, in Adding Value to Livestock Diversity
sources.note: LPP, LIFE Network, IUCN-WISP and FAO, 2010, printed pages 99 to 102; Puntland study based on projects in 2001 to 2007. Specific local evidence rather than a timeless rule for all Somalis.

sources.title: UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning: Somali Distance Education and Literacy
sources.note: 2014 programme assessment: radio lessons and named learner testimonies. Halimo’s Hargeisa home is in Somaliland; place is not used as a sovereignty claim.

sources.title: UNICEF Somalia: Menstrual management is not a secret
sources.note: 2 April 2024 report, Godod School in Mudug, PMWDO lessons, Nafiso’s experience and school water/sanitation services.

sources.title: UNESCO: Protecting Somalia’s documentary heritage
sources.note: 22 June 2026 account of preservation workshop and Radio Mogadishu’s approximately 45,000 tapes. Archive evidence only; the article’s compressed campaign chronology is not used.
